_comment: A fixture registry for tests/test_tree_counts.py, in the shape guardrails/tree-counts.json carries. Its measurements read guardrails/tree-count-fixtures/tree, a small tree a test owns outright. An `argv` here is run exactly the way a real one is, so an edit to one of these argument lists changes what a test measures and is reviewed the way a change to a check script is reviewed (SPEC R306, INV-305).

homes.text: The fixture tree holds {fixture_lines} lines of text across its files. Count them yourself with `cat tree/*.txt | wc -l`; a run of the gate over this fixture is refused where that command disagrees with the number printed here. The number decides how much text a fixture run reads, and it is read against the two files this fixture tree ships. It holds at five lines, and the direction to hold is down: when it rises, every fixture run reads more text than the case needs.

homes.template: {n} lines stand in the fixture tree.

ground.counts: lines of text in the files of the fixture tree
ground.decision: how much text a fixture run of the gate reads
ground.on_move: every fixture run reads more text or less
ground.compared_to: the two files this fixture tree ships
ground.target: five lines, the size the cases here are written against

homes.template: More than three lines stand in the fixture tree.

ground.counts: lines of text in the files of the fixture tree, read as a floor
ground.decision: whether the fixture tree still carries enough text for the at-least case to mean anything
ground.on_move: the floor case stops proving what it was written to prove

compared_to.reason: a floor is read against itself; no second figure stands beside it here

better.reason: a fixture tree that grows costs a run more time and one that shrinks below the floor stops carrying the case, so neither direction is better on its own

ground.target: at or above three lines, the floor this fixture publishes
